one_line: Kerala mathematician-astronomer of the Parangngottu family, author of the Malayalam treatise Yuktibhāṣā in the 16th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s, lean and scholarly with a calm, upright posture.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium brown Kerala complexion, sharp thoughtful eyes with slightly thick brows, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, default expression a soft focused gaze as if working through a calculation.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair, shoulder-length and slightly wavy, oiled and combed back, gathered into a low knot at the nape; simple off-white cotton headcloth (mundu-turban style) wrapped once around the head with a small tail tucked at the back.
appearance.costume: Traditional 16th‑century Kerala Brahmin attire: an off‑white cotton uttariyam (upper cloth) draped over both shoulders and around the torso, covering chest and back modestly, with a clean fold over the left shoulder; a cream-colored ankle-length cotton dhoti/mundu with a thin golden kasavu border, wrapped and pleated in front, tied securely at the waist; bare forearms but wrists adorned with two slender bronze bangles; a simple tulasi bead mala around the neck; small gold stud earrings; plain leather sandals on the feet; textiles are matte, slightly textured handwoven cotton with subtle vertical weave lines, no printed patterns beyond the single kasavu border line.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle of Yuktibhāṣā bound with a thin coir cord, held in his left hand, and a slender stylus (iron or brass) for inscribing on palm leaves in his right hand.

ref_desc: Jyeṣṭhadeva is a lean late‑forties Kerala scholar with an oval medium‑brown face, shoulder‑length black hair in a low knot under an off‑white headcloth, wearing off‑white uttariyam and cream mundu with golden border, bronze bangles and tulasi mala, carrying a palm‑leaf manuscript bundle and stylus in off‑white, cream, golden yellow and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Jyeṣṭhadeva: a lean late‑forties Kerala mathematician with an oval medium-brown face, sharp thoughtful eyes, straight nose, and short beard and moustache, his shoulder-length black hair combed back into a low knot under a simple off-white cotton headcloth. Show him in 16th-century Kerala Brahmin attire: an off-white cotton uttariyam draped over both shoulders and around the torso, modestly covering chest and back, its main fold resting over the left shoulder; a cream ankle-length cotton mundu/dhoti with a single thin golden kasavu border, wrapped and pleated in front and tied at the waist, with subtle handwoven texture. Add two slender bronze bangles on his wrists, a tulasi bead mala around his neck, small gold stud earrings, and plain brown leather sandals. In his left hand he holds a bound bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts, and in his right hand a slender stylus used for inscribing, posed in a calm, focused stance. Use a palette dominated by off-white, cream, golden yellow, and warm brown, with simple, historically grounded details and no modern or fantastical elements.
